quests.storyParagraph: Dr. Voss needed the lab's mass spectrometer to analyze twelve samples for a paper due at the end of the month. The instrument could be booked only by users who had completed a safety refresher. The refresher ran on Wednesdays, and she attended the next one. With her certificate in hand, she reserved the earliest slot, which was five days away. The samples had to be prepared no more than two days before measurement. She therefore held off preparing them until the slot was near. She prepared the samples and ran the analysis on the reserved day. The data reached her co-author in time for the draft.

quests.storyParagraph: Film student Rafaela wanted to shoot a scene on a bridge. The city would grant a filming permit only if neighboring residents consented. quests.storyParagraph: The IT team planned to migrate the payroll system on a weekend. Finance had a freeze on system changes during month-end processing. Payroll ran normally on Monday.

quests.storyParagraph: Bea was cooking dinner for guests, and everything had to be hot at the same moment. The lamb needed most of the afternoon in a moderate oven. Near the end of the lamb's roasting time, she turned the oven up and added the potatoes. She moved the lamb to the counter to rest under foil while the potatoes finished. Meat and potatoes reached the table together.

quests.storyParagraph: The charity planned a gala for two hundred guests at a historic hall. The hall's fire limit allowed only one hundred and fifty people. The board considered a second sitting. A second sitting required extra staff and a second round of catering. The caterer said they could handle it only with two weeks' notice. The board approved the second sitting the same day, meeting the notice period. The charity re-sent invitations assigning guests to sittings. Responses came in, and a few guests swapped sittings. Both sittings sold out, and the gala raised twice the previous year's total.
